html:
Argentina legalised same-sex marriage in July 2010, the first country in Latin America to do so and the tenth in the world. The Senate passed the law on 15 July by 33 votes to 27 after an all night debate, and President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner signed it on 21 July.

The law gave same-sex couples the same rights as other married couples, adoption included. The Catholic Church, led in Buenos Aires by Cardinal Jorge Bergoglio, later Pope Francis, campaigned hard against it, and church groups held large rallies. Buenos Aires had allowed civil unions since 2002.

Argentina went further in 2012 with a gender identity law that let people change their legal sex without approval from a doctor or judge. The region followed: Uruguay and Brazil in 2013, then Colombia, Ecuador, Chile and Mexico. That a mostly Catholic country led the way made the law a turning point for Latin America.
